title: Cistercian 1606, Canon Missæ: complete strict Canon constituent
scope: Complete strict Eucharistic Canon constituent of the Paris 1606 Cistercian missal: from the printed CANON MISSÆ. heading and Te igitur on printed p.190, BSB canvas244/full-provider-PDF 245, through Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen. on printed p.197 left, canvas251/PDF252, immediately before Orémus/Præcéptis/Pater noster. All five printed seasonal Communicantes insertions and the Pascha/Pentecost Hanc igitur insertion, their rubrics, continuation signs, name cues and 26 crosses are included in source order. The fourth page in this sequence is BSB-labelled193 but actually misprinted 192. The later Ordinary under the same Canon Missæ running head is explicitly outside this strict Canon. Whole-book and complete-Ordinary coverage remain partial; this constituent is independent of the unchanged accepted offertory and inherits no wording from another edition.
transcribed_by: AI original-image source transcriber (Paris 1606 strict Canon preparation)
excluded_book_divisions: All preceding preparations, Creed, offertory, prefaces and the illustration/preceding material on printed p.189
Printed p.197 below the final Canon Amen: Orémus, Præcéptis salutáribus and beginning of Pater noster; all of p.197 right column
Later Ordinary, Communion, closing prayers and the appended Suffragium on printed pp.198–200, despite their Canon Missæ running head
Sanctorale beginning printed p.201, calendar, propers, lectionary and every other book division
Running-head repetitions, foliation, catchwords, ornament, ink colour, page geometry and chant notation; sung words inside the bounds are retained

evidence.locus: Unnumbered title page, BSB canvas1: Paris Marnef/Cavellat imprint1606

completeness_evidence.locus: Eight complete source images, strict Canon from heading/Te igitur to final Per omnia/Amen; final-page lower-left and right-column Ordinary excluded

units.normalization: Direct source reading of original BSB 1606 scans: long s becomes s; split display initials merge in sentence case; source line wraps and line-end word divisions join inside semantic blocks. Printed nasal suspension bars, the standard -us brevigraph, -q;/-que suspension and Dñi contraction are expanded without adding absent accents. The marked vir- contraction in the Nativity insertion is expanded as unaccented virginis; no acute is inferred from the separately printed main Communicantes form. Printed u/v, j, æ/œ, actual accents, case within sentences, punctuation, parentheses, ampersands, N. placeholders and abbreviated rubric/variant endings remain. Red crosses are serialized as ✠, including crosses inside words; printed asterisks remain *. Rubrics are separate units. Communicantes opening and continuation remain separate around the five proper insertions, preserving column/source order. The source’s duplicated & & in Supplices and Easter diem sacratíssimam are retained. No familiar Roman wording or missing ending is supplied. The 35 UTF-8 NFC semantic units retain source order. The main Communicantes continuation preserves three source paragraphs, separated by a blank LF line; its selected physical-line range includes those two blank lines. Other units occupy one physical line. The complete artifact ends with LF; each unit selection hash excludes its terminating LF. Running heads after the opening title, page numbers, catchwords, ornament, type colour, line/column geometry and chant notes are recorded as facsimile/paratext rather than text; all sung words within the Canon, including its final Amen, remain. This is a normalized reading transcription, not a glyph-diplomatic or musical edition.
